text.aura: Your aura is a polished jewel catching light. Sin carries a refined, elegant presence that people notice instantly, even if they can't name exactly what's special. You read as stylish, sensitive and a little bit precious, in the good sense: someone with taste, standards and a quiet sparkle. Your glow is about detail and quality. A perfectly chosen ring, a beautiful turn of phrase, the way you hold a cup of coffee. People often find you intriguing and slightly out of reach. The glow-up for you isn't about polishing more. You're already polished. It's about letting a bit of imperfection and warmth show, so people feel invited closer instead of admiring you from behind glass.
text.how-people-read-you: First impression: elegant, put-together, possibly aloof. People assume you have great taste and high standards, and they're right. Some feel slightly nervous around you, worried they won't measure up. Once they know you, they discover a sensitive, witty, deeply loyal person who notices beautiful small things. The misreading comes from that polish. Some think you're cold, judgmental or high-maintenance, when you're actually just private and careful with your feelings. To be read more accurately, show your humour early, compliment others generously, and let people see you a little messy sometimes, laughing too hard, admitting something embarrassing. You'll still sparkle. But people will feel the warmth, not just the shine.
text.colors: Your home palette is refined Metal: pearl white, champagne, soft silver, dove grey, icy pastels like lavender and powder blue. These look elegant and luminous on you, like moonlight on silk. Earth supports Metal, so soft beige, nude and stone tones make wonderful bases. Deep Water colours, navy and midnight, add a sophisticated, mysterious edge for evenings. Jewellery is your playground: delicate silver, pearls, a single perfect stone. Be careful with very loud, warm colours like bright orange or chaotic prints. They can drown your refined glow and make you look uncomfortable. Your best palette feels like an expensive perfume bottle, clean, luminous and quietly special.
text.style: Your style is elegant minimalism with jewellery as the star. Clean silhouettes, quality fabrics, silk, fine knit, crisp cotton, and accessories that look carefully chosen. You look incredible in monochrome outfits with one stunning detail. Think slip skirts, tailored trousers, fine-gauge sweaters, a structured small bag. You understand fit and finish better than most souls. The trap is perfectionism: overthinking every outfit, feeling uncomfortable unless everything is flawless, avoiding photos on "bad" days. Allow some ease. A slightly messy bun, a relaxed weekend look, an imperfect candid shot. Your best photo is soft daylight, close-up, with jewellery visible and a real smile, not your controlled one.
text.vibe: Your glow-up vibe is the approachable jewel. Imagine the elegant webtoon character everyone thinks is untouchable, until one chapter shows her laughing with crumbs on her face, and readers fall for her completely. The shift for you is warmth and spontaneity. Say yes to a plan without checking if your outfit is perfect. Share something you're proud of without downplaying it. Give compliments as freely as you notice flaws. Laugh loudly once in a while. Let someone see you without the polish. Your elegance is real and it isn't going anywhere. Adding warmth just turns it from something people admire into something people feel lucky to be close to.
text.aura-dims: Your aura dims when you feel criticized, overlooked or under pressure to be perfect. You start overanalyzing your appearance, your messages, every small thing you said, and your glow turns anxious. You might withdraw, look tense or go icy-polite. Your style can become either obsessively perfect or completely abandoned. The reset is gentle and sensory. Clean and tidy your space, because order calms you. Take a long, unhurried bath or shower with something that smells beautiful. Put on your favourite piece of jewellery even if you're staying home. Spend time with someone who adores you exactly as you are. Unfollow accounts that make you compare yourself. A jewel shines brightest when it's handled gently.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, your aura is a jewel. Elegant, luminous, people notice you without knowing why.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And then they're scared to talk to you. You look like you'd judge their shoes.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Pearl, champagne, soft silver. You look like expensive perfume.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also changed your outfit four times this morning. For a grocery run.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your glow-up is warmth. Let people see you laugh with crumbs on your face.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Perfect is boring. Post the candid one.

spring.intro: Spring hands a Sin jewel a garden full of Wood to judge, since Metal controls Wood, so your aura is refined, curious and quietly evaluating everything. People read you as elegant and selective, possibly a little picky about the coffee. You likely enjoy fresh pastels and delicate prints, and you wear them precisely. Your glow-up is security and sparkle. Earth, your resource, gives champagne, cream and soft beige as a luxurious base, and silver or pearl details let your Metal shine. Keep one fresh green or floral piece for the season so you look part of the garden, not above it. The spring Sin glow is a pearl ring on a garden table.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Sin, you look like you're judging the brunch. Add one floral. Join the garden.

summer.intro: Summer Fire is the element that controls Metal, and a jewel left in heat feels it, so a summer Sin aura is dazzling, sensitive and easily scratched by a harsh comment. People read you as refined and expressive, but you can feel overexposed in loud rooms. Bright red and orange in large doses overpower your shine. Your glow-up is shade and protection. Earth softens Fire and supports Metal, so sand, stone and soft taupe work beautifully, and Water blues cool the whole look. Choose smooth, high-quality fabrics and one exquisite metal piece rather than five pretty ones. The summer Sin glow is a diamond in a shaded courtyard, sparkling without fighting the sun.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Sin, soft taupe and one perfect silver earring. You shine best in the shade.

autumn.intro: Metal is in command in autumn, so a Sin jewel born then is in its element. Your aura reads as polished, poised and quietly luxurious, the person who always looks put together even at the airport. You likely own perfect white shirts and delicate jewellery already. The risk is looking untouchable, more showroom than person. Your glow-up is flow and expression. Water, your output, brings midnight blue and fluid silhouettes, making you approachable without losing elegance. Add one personal object with a story, a vintage ring or a charm someone gave you. The autumn Sin glow is a jewel seen by candlelight: precious, and suddenly warm enough to touch.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Sin, you look like a showroom. Wear your grandmother's ring. Be a person.

winter.intro: Winter's Water flows out of Metal, and classical saju loves a Sin jewel washed in clear water, so a winter Sin aura is crisp, luminous and articulate. People read you as calm, clever and slightly cool. Midnight blue and black look sensational on you, but they can make you seem far away, like a beautiful window display behind glass. Your glow-up is warmth with a soft base. Earth, your resource, adds cream, camel and soft gold. Fire brings a flash of rose or warm red. A cream knit with silver earrings is your signature winter look. The winter Sin glow is frost on glass at sunrise: clear, bright, and touched with warmth.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Sin, a cream knit and silver earrings. Frost at sunrise, and everyone notices.

strength.strong: A strong Sin Metal aura is a jewel in a museum case: flawless, admired and untouchable. With plenty of Metal and Earth, you look polished, refined and very deliberate, and people may feel underdressed beside you even at a picnic. The blind spot is perfectionism. Your look can feel so curated that nobody risks getting close. Add Water for ease and Wood for life: a relaxed silk, a sea-blue tone, a natural linen or raw cotton. Let one detail be imperfect on purpose, a rolled sleeve or a mismatched earring. Precious feels warmer when it is a little lived-in.
strength.weak: A weak Sin Metal aura is a gem left in a drawer. With little Metal or Earth support, you have exquisite taste but don't quite trust it, so you wear safe, ordinary clothes and keep your favourite pieces for occasions that never seem to arrive. The blind spot is shrinking your shine to avoid looking like you tried. Your glow-up is wearing the good things now: the silver earrings, the silk blouse, the white coat you were saving. Treat an ordinary Wednesday as an occasion worth dressing for. You were made to catch the light.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood gives your aura lots of drive and upward energy, but it can read as restless or intense, always busy, always growing. Your style may lean practical and outdoorsy, sometimes at the expense of polish. Balance it with Metal touches: a crisp white shirt, silver jewellery, cleaner lines, one tailored piece. Declutter your wardrobe so what remains feels intentional. Your glow is strongest when your ambition looks calm, like a tall tree that doesn't need to prove it's growing.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means your aura can lack a sense of freshness and new beginnings. You might stick to the same outfits for years or feel unsure about trying new styles. Bring in Wood: greens, botanical prints, natural fabrics like linen and cotton, plants in your space. Try one new style element each month, a different silhouette, a new accessory, a new hair clip. Growth looks good on you. Let your style evolve a little, the way spring changes a garden.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your aura bright, bold and sometimes overwhelming. You might gravitate to loud colours, big statements and high-energy looks that occasionally feel like too much at once. Balance it with Water: navy, deep blue, black accents, calmer silhouettes. Choose one statement per outfit instead of five. Let some quiet into your presence too, listening more, moving slower. Your glow is already strong. Cooling it slightly makes it look richer and more confident.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means your aura can feel understated, sometimes so understated that people overlook you. You might default to neutrals and avoid anything that draws attention. Bring in Fire: a red lip, a coral scarf, warm gold jewellery, a little shimmer. Seek out sunlight in photos and in life. Let yourself be seen in small ways: post the photo, wear the bright thing, laugh openly. Visibility is a skill, and it looks lovely on you when you allow it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth gives you a grounded, warm aura that can slide into heavy or overly practical. Your wardrobe may be comfortable but samey, lots of beige, brown and safe basics. Balance it with Wood: fresh greens, lighter fabrics, a playful print, something that moves when you walk. Try one unexpected piece. Rearrange your space for a fresh feeling. Your stability is beautiful. A little lightness on top keeps it from looking stuck.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth can make your aura feel scattered or ungrounded, lots of ideas, many style moods, not much consistency. Your outfits may change wildly depending on your mood. Bring in Earth: camel, beige, warm brown, ochre, and solid basics like a good coat and reliable shoes. Build a small capsule wardrobe you can trust. Ceramics, wood and warm lighting at home help too. When your foundation is steady, your creativity looks intentional instead of chaotic.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives your aura sharpness and polish that can tip into cold or severe. Your style may be immaculate but a little untouchable: very clean lines, lots of black, white and grey, everything controlled. Balance it with Fire: warm colours near your face, soft textures, a smile that comes sooner. Let one thing be imperfect on purpose, rolled sleeves, tousled hair, a playful accessory. Precision is your strength. Warmth makes it inviting.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal can make your aura feel soft but a little undefined. People like you, but they might not remember your style clearly. Bring in Metal: silver jewellery, crisp white, sharp tailoring, clean shoes, a structured bag. Edit your wardrobe so every piece earns its place. A clear signature, the same ring, the same scent, a consistent colour, gives your look definition. Clarity doesn't make you colder. It makes you memorable.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water gives your aura depth and mystery, but it can read as distant, moody or hard to reach. You might hide in dark colours and oversized layers. Balance it with Earth: warm neutrals near your face, structured pieces, a grounded silhouette. Add a little Fire too, a coral or rose accent, to bring warmth. Let people see your expression clearly. Your mystery is magnetic. A bit of warmth makes it feel welcoming, not unreachable.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means your aura can feel busy and bright without much depth or calm. You might always be on, always moving, with little stillness. Bring in Water: navy, midnight blue, black, flowing fabrics, a more relaxed silhouette. Create quiet moments in your day and let them show in your style, softer textures, fewer accessories. Water by your bed and slow evenings help your energy settle. Depth looks good on you. Give it some room.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: hiking boots, three plants and a tote bag. Add one sharp silver thing.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your freshness is gorgeous. A crisp white shirt makes it look intentional.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: red bag, gold chain, leopard coat. Pick one. The others can wait.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your warmth is your magic. Let navy or stone frame it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: beige, oatmeal, sand, more beige. You look like a very calm cupboard.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is beautiful. One silver piece or a deep blue lifts it.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: you look expensive and impossible to talk to. Add one soft texture.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your polish is stunning. A warm knit lets people come closer.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: all black, all mystery, all the time. Even vampires wear burgundy.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is magnetic. A warm colour helps people find the door.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Try a sage scarf or a leafy print. Let your style grow a little.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Same outfit since 2021 isn't a signature. It's a rut with good lighting.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? A coral scarf or warm gold earrings changes how people greet you.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: Head-to-toe grey says 'don't notice me'. Is that really the message?

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? A camel coat or a terracotta bag grounds your whole look.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Five trends this month, zero signature. Commit to something longer than a week.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? A crisp white shirt or a silver cuff gives your look clean edges.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Everything slightly creased and slightly oversized reads accidental. Tailor one piece.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? Deep navy or a fluid silk adds calm depth to your look.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Always bright, always on. Let one outfit be quiet. People lean in.
